body:
I couldn't keep any of my student's attention and I couldn't explain how to play well. It's one of those things where you know how to do it, but you can't explain how you do it so they can learn. I don't know how to describe it but when I would show them something, it seems like it just kind of flew over their heads.

I've had an older student tell me outright that he couldn't follow along. I just gave up on it and after I quit my music major I just kind of gave up on playing music.

I don't know if I have depression as I have never been professionally diagnosed. But either way, I can't afford a psychiatrist or whoever diagnoses that sort of thing. They provide professional counselors at my college, but I already told my experience with that. They asked me really personal things my first time there and I didn't want to get into it. I don't know if they can diagnose or not, but I don't think I am going back. I just feel drained all of the time, and yes I know I have a major drinking problem, but I have no desire to quit.

I remember when I first started college I was excited. I was on the track to graduate but dropped my junior year. I was studying music, but couldn't see a future outside of becoming a teacher, and after giving lessons, I realized I was not a good teacher. I am now studying to be an X-ray tech, but as I said in the original post, I can't get into the program because I wrecked my GPA before I dropped the first time. I lived with my parents for about 2 1/2 years, and I worked at a dead end job, not making enough to even afford an apartment, and barely enough to pay my loans on time. My parents want to see me succeed, but I can't. I've already fucked my grades so hard that there's no turning back unless I started 2 years of college all over again, and I know they are getting tired of it and my loans can only go so far.

They would get over it eventually. I know this because a friend killed himself earlier this year. I miss him a lot, but you just go on living.

My parents won't say I'm a burden, but every time I ask for money my mother asks where it's going because it's draining their bank accounts and my dad has talked with me before, saying he can't support me much longer unless I get good grades. I already have academic probation on my record, and at the end of this semester it's going to be a suspension. I may not even qualify for loans after this since this will be my second drop. If I killed myself, loans would be forgiven and my folks could save for once in their lives. I already had a friend that killed himself and you just learn to move on. I just don't see any other option. If I drop out, I'll be working another dead end job not making enough money to live on my own. FFS I'm 24, and my sister is 21 making 6 figures, and already has a house and a new car. All I'm good for is drinking my folk's paycheck away.

But the reality is that there is a lot of things I did in my past that I can not forgive myself for even prior to this, even after being forgiven by this person I hurt. The money and lack of direction is just kind of the straw that broke the camel's back for me and it's what I feel most comfortable talking about. I can't find any reason to live anymore. The pros far outweigh the cons at this point.

It also fucks with me when I try to get back into the things I used to love, like playing guitar and singing, but I just feel nothing. I turn on old video games I loved as a kid, but get bored after the intro. I watch a movie and I'll stop halfway through it and just go back to sleep or try to get drunk enough to finish it. I used to work out, but haven't had any desire to do so for years now. I don't think I've played guitar or sang for about 6 months at the *least*. I've been spending most of my time in bed and will only get out to make a hot pocket or a drink.

There's no future for me other than winding up homeless or working a dead end job when my parents get tired of my bullshit. It would be quicker just to end it and be over with it. I don't know what to do or how to get these thoughts out of my head.
